newsitem.title: HONDURAS: ACPC coffee growers step up origin offensive.
newsitem.headline: ACPC coffee growers step up origin offensive.

text.p: Central American bloc nations of Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) stepped up Tuesday their continuing battle on how to classify coffee origins.

One of the points agreed at the regional ACPC meeting here in the heart of Honduras' most spectacular Mayan ruins was for members to pressure their government to take a firm stance against consumer nation moves to have coffee classified by where it is processed. ACPC members want coffee standardised by where it is grown.
"The fight is going to be easy, it is just a matter of putting the juridical house in order," Salvadoran coffee delegate Herbert De Sola said here.
"Origin means where it comes from not where someone turns it into something else," he said, adding it would be absurb for the world suddenly starting to see "Icelandic coffee".
One of the decisions taken at the two-day gathering here was for each member nation to press their governments to lobby the World Trade Organisation on the issue.
Central American bloc nations of the ACPC are Honduras, El Salvador, Costa Rica, Nicaragau and Ecuador. Colombia also attended this meeting as special guest.
